displayQuote: A champion is someone who gets up when they can't

meta.title: Who really said "A champion is someone who gets up when they can't"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Widely pinned on boxer Jack Dempsey. The exact words trace to no primary source — but they condense a real, documented Dempsey remark about getting up as a hungry fighter.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'A champion is someone who gets up when they can't'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Jack Dempsey. No speech or book pins the exact wording, but it faithfully paraphrases a documented Dempsey line recorded by Grantland Rice.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Widely and plausibly credited to Dempsey, and squarely consistent with his own words — but no speech, book, interview, or letter pins this exact aphorism to him. It reads as a polished condensation of a genuinely documented Dempsey remark, recorded by sportswriter Grantland Rice, about having to get up off the canvas as a young “hungry fighter.”

source.heading: The closest documented source

docMeta.dd: Grantland Rice, Book of Boxing, p. 299

source.excerpt: When I was a young fellow I was knocked down plenty. I wanted to stay down, but I couldn’t. I had to collect the two dollars for winning or go hungry. I had to get up. I was one of those hungry fighters.
trail: Wikiquote’s Jack Dempsey page ↗ lists the aphorism, but its only citation is a now-defunct boxing-promoter article — not a speech, book, or interview.
The same page carries a properly sourced Dempsey remark on the identical theme (“I had to get up… one of those hungry fighters”), attributed to Grantland Rice’s Book of Boxing, p. 299 ↗.
Quote Investigator ↗ has not examined this exact line; its nearest “champion” entry traces a different saying to Wilma Rudolph, confirming this wording has no rigorous origin trail.
source.excerptNote: This is the documented Dempsey passage — recorded by sportswriter Grantland Rice — that the popular one-line aphorism appears to condense. The crisp wording “a champion is someone who gets up when they can’t” is not found in this or any other primary Dempsey source.
source.rightsNote: The polished aphorism has no identifiable first publication, so no copyright status can honestly be asserted for it. The documented remark it appears to condense was recorded by Grantland Rice (Book of Boxing, p. 299), a mid-20th-century work that would itself remain under copyright.

author.name: Jack Dempsey
author.heading: About Jack Dempsey
author.bio: William Harrison “Jack” Dempsey, nicknamed the “Manassa Mauler,” held the world heavyweight title from 1919 to 1926 and became one of the defining sports celebrities of the Roaring Twenties. He grew up in hardscrabble poverty in Colorado and fought in saloons and mining camps for small purses — the lived experience behind his often-quoted line about getting up because he “had to collect the two dollars for winning or go hungry.” His blend of ferocity and hard-won resilience made him a natural magnet for perseverance sayings.

cite.sourceCitation: Earliest reliably documented in the related form: Grantland Rice, quoting Jack Dempsey, Book of Boxing, p. 299 (“I had to get up. I was one of those hungry fighters.”). The exact aphorism “A champion is someone who gets up when they can’t” has no located primary source.

misattribution.heading: Attribution & wording check
misattribution.intro: This is not a case of the wrong name — the sentiment really is Dempsey’s. The problem is the words: the memorable one-liner that circulates is an untraceable paraphrase, not a documented quotation.

items.why: The crisp aphorism appears on quote-aggregator sites and, per Wikiquote ↗, is backed only by a now-dead boxing-promoter web article — not by any speech, book, interview, or letter of Dempsey’s.
Dempsey really did voice this idea: “I wanted to stay down, but I couldn’t… I had to get up,” recorded by Grantland Rice ↗ (Book of Boxing, p. 299).
The line circulates as both “gets up when he can’t” and “gets up when they can’t” — a sign of an oral, aggregated saying with no fixed printed original.

misattribution.truthLine: Dempsey’s documented words were about a hungry young fighter forced off the canvas; the polished “a champion is someone who gets up when they can’t” is a faithful but unsourced paraphrase — see Wikiquote ↗.

context.heading: Why it rings true
lead: Dempsey is an unusually fitting home for this saying, which is part of why it sticks. He came up fighting in Colorado saloons and mining camps for a few dollars a bout, and his own account of resilience — getting up because staying down meant going hungry — is one of the most repeated things he ever said. The aphorism simply files that raw memory down to a motto.

That fit is exactly what makes the wording hard to police. A line that sounds like something Dempsey would say, attached to a name synonymous with never quitting, spreads faster than any citation can keep up with — which is how a genuine sentiment ends up circulating as a quotation nobody can source.
context.pull: A real Dempsey memory, filed down into a motto no primary source records.
